entities.description: Baptist congregation in Chicago founded by Great Migration arrivals; documented site of mass feeding, civic hosting, gospel music, and cross-congregational talent circulation.
entities.name: Morning Star Baptist Church of Chicago

entities.description: Historic Black Baptist church in Chicago; center of the gospel music system under Thomas A. Dorsey; archive destroyed in 2006 fire.
entities.name: Pilgrim Baptist Church

entities.description: Chicago Baptist congregation; its 1915 souvenir program is cited in Miles Mark Fisher's church history, evidencing the anniversary-program genre in Chicago.
entities.name: Olivet Baptist Church of Chicago

entities.description: FSA photographer; made the V01 photograph 'Pastor of the Pentecostal Church, Chicago, Illinois.'
entities.name: Russell Lee

entities.description: Gospel composer and music director; founded a Black gospel publishing firm; co-founded the National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses (1932). Treated here as music-system infrastructure.
entities.name: Thomas A. Dorsey

entities.description: Gospel trio nurtured in the Morning Star choir from childhood; talent circulated between Morning Star and Pilgrim Baptist.
entities.name: The Barrett Sisters

entities.description: Gospel singer and educator; featured in 'Say Amen, Somebody' alongside Dorsey.
entities.name: Willie Mae Ford Smith

entities.description: Organization co-founded by Thomas A. Dorsey; standardized and circulated gospel choir practice.
entities.name: National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses

entities.description: Received money, sleeping accommodations, and meals from Morning Star Baptist Church; partner in migrant support.
entities.name: Chicago Urban League

entities.description: Held lectures at Morning Star; evidence of the church building as a political meeting space.
entities.name: Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA)

entities.description: Hosted at Morning Star; evidence of health-training activity inside the church.
entities.name: Black Cross Nurses

entities.description: Scholar; author of 'Passionately Human, No Less Divine: Religion and Culture in Black Chicago, 1915-1952' (2005), the brief's central migration-religion frame.
entities.name: Wallace D. Best

entities.description: Author of 'Labor of Love, Labor of Sorrow' (1985); broader scholarship on Black women's labor and family, including Chicago employers' kitchens.
entities.name: Jacqueline Jones

entities.description: Scholar cited for Black working-class women's labor struggles; 2015 article indexed as source of the Roosevelt Hotel maids episode (full citation unverified).
entities.name: Keona K. Ervin

entities.description: Chicago family informant ('Uncle Don') describing Sunday gatherings with potato salad, collard greens, fried chicken, grace, and a large table; single-family oral-history-style source.
entities.name: Uncle Don (family informant)

entities.description: UChicago archival and community-engagement initiative founded 2005 by Jacqueline Stewart; preserves South Side home movies 1929-1980s.
entities.name: South Side Home Movie Project

entities.description: Site of the documented 1930s dispute in which six Black maids demanded all Sundays off and walked out (PROVISIONAL; citation unverified).
entities.name: Roosevelt Hotel
